newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker after lackluster session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker after lackluster session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker in lackluster, rangebound trading after red metal futures on both sides of the Atlantic reopened after public holidays Monday.
COMEX July copper settled 0.35 cent weaker at 118.40 cents per pound, traded 118.60 to 117.50 cents.
Copper looked well within overbought territory last week after rapid, strong gains to just shy of 120.00 cents in the July contract.
Retracement and consolidation were inevitable, dealers said.
The 9-day and 14-day RSI has fallen to 76 and 72, down from about 80 last week, but still in overbought areas.
LME stocks continue to fall, down 650 tonnes Tuesday to 137,025 tonnes, providing underpinning to the price advance.
COMEX stocks on Tuesday rose 1,907 short tons to 42,397 short tons.
London's cash to three months premium or backwardation was stable at $70/$75.
Tuesday, supervisors at Chile Copper Co's huge Chuquicamata mine cast their ballots in a strike vote, and the result was due some time after 2200 GMT.
